quick: Take with water; may give with food
summary: Levamisole is an imidazothiazole anthelmintic, classically used as a single dose for Ascaris lumbricoides (roundworm) and hookworm infection, and also as a steroid-sparing immunomodulator in relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome in children. It is no longer FDA-approved for human use in the US (formerly used as an adjuvant in colon cancer; withdrawn), so this record is based on WHO/EMA/BNF and standard references. The major safety concern with repeated/immunomodulatory use is agranulocytosis, which mandates blood-count monitoring.
indications: Steroid-sparing immunomodulation in frequently-relapsing or steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome (children) - specialist use

dosage.d: 150 mg as a single oral dose
~2.5-3 mg/kg as a single oral dose
dosage.n: Repeat after 7 days if heavy infection

dosage.d: Single dose as for ascariasis; may repeat after ~7 days
dosage.n: Higher cure rates with repeat dosing

admin: Give as a single oral dose with water; can be taken with food
No purgative or fasting is required for anthelmintic use
For nephrotic syndrome, use only under specialist supervision with regular blood-count monitoring
Counsel on hygiene/sanitation to prevent re-infection
moa: As an anthelmintic, levamisole acts as a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist at the worm's neuromuscular junction, causing sustained muscle depolarization and spastic (tonic) paralysis of the parasite, which is then expelled. As an immunomodulator it appears to restore depressed cell-mediated immune function (T-cell/phagocyte activity), the basis of its steroid-sparing effect.

absolute: History of agranulocytosis caused by levamisole
monitor: Complete blood count (agranulocytosis/neutropenia) with repeated or immunomodulatory use

preg: Avoid unless clearly necessary; human safety data in pregnancy are limited. Defer treatment of asymptomatic helminth infection where possible.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding; data on transfer into milk are limited.
renal: Use with caution and consider dose reduction in significant renal impairment, as elimination may be reduced.
hepatic: Levamisole is metabolized in the liver; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Myelosuppressive drugs - additive risk of agranulocytosis/neutropenia
Warfarin - levamisole may potentiate the anticoagulant effect; monitor INR
moderate: Phenytoin - levamisole can raise phenytoin levels
minor: Other anthelmintics - generally not combined routinely
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, nausea) can occur.
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause neutropenia/agranulocytosis on CBC; monitor blood counts.

serious: Vasculitis (cutaneous, sometimes with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies)
emergency: Signs of agranulocytosis: high fever, severe sore throat, mouth ulcers, infection

monitoring: Complete blood count, especially with repeated or immunomodulatory dosing (watch for agranulocytosis)
Fever, sore throat or other signs of infection
Renal and hepatic function with prolonged use
Stool examination to confirm cure where appropriate
counsel: Take the single dose as directed; maintain good hygiene to prevent re-infection
Seek urgent care if you develop fever, sore throat or mouth ulcers (possible blood-count problem)
Report rash, numbness, or persistent vomiting
With repeated/long-term use for kidney disease, keep all blood-test appointments
pk: Rapid anthelmintic effect; worms cleared within ~1-2 days
Plasma peak ~1.5-2 h after an oral dose
Single dose usually sufficient for roundworm
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: No longer FDA-approved for human use in the US (former colon-cancer adjuvant use withdrawn); this record uses WHO/EMA/BNF and standard references
AGRANULOCYTOSIS is the key serious risk - monitor CBC with repeated or immunomodulatory dosing
Single-dose anthelmintic for ascariasis; albendazole/mebendazole are now more commonly used first-line
Used as a steroid-sparing agent in childhood nephrotic syndrome under specialist care
Levamisole is a notorious adulterant of illicit cocaine and a cause of cocaine-associated vasculitis/neutropenia
missed: For single-dose anthelmintic therapy, take the dose when remembered. For alternate-day immunomodulatory regimens, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the next dose, then skip it - do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause vomiting, agitation, confusion, seizures and (with large or repeated doses) agranulocytosis. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care, monitor blood counts and treat seizures with benzodiazepines.
